title: introduce-tailor-microtemplate-typed-toolchain-playground
author: Priya Raman
description:
Motivation: add a compact, opinionated RAG microtemplate (codename 'tailor') that demonstrates typed tool contracts, progressive offline indexing, and a lightweight dev replay server for iterative local development. This is targeted at engineers who want a batteries-included example that spans: 1) authoring a typed tool contract; 2) a small Kotlin client showing production-like typed bindings; 3) a TypeScript playground shim for quick iteration; 4) an offline indexer with incremental patching and language-detection; 5) CI smoke tests and a snapshot replay devserver for deterministic e2e checks.

Summary of changes: added a new examples/tailor microtemplate with README and runnable quickstart; introduced a typed tool contract spec (YAML + TS/KT bindings); added Kotlin example client and TS playground; implemented a tiny offline indexer that supports incremental patches and language-aware embedding profiles; added snapshot-replay devserver to scripts/dev-server for deterministic authoring and CI e2e; docs site snippet and quickstart page included under docs/site/snippets for discoverability.

Why this is different: most RAG examples focus on orchestration or large playbooks. Tailor is intentionally compact (~20 files) and focuses on developer ergonomics: typed contracts to prevent runtime tool-call drift, replayable devserver to remove flakiness when authoring prompts, and progressive offline indexing for faster local loops. It includes both a Kotlin client (to show a typed, JVM-first integration path for mobile/platform teams) and a TypeScript playground (for rapid iteration and demoing in the browser).

How to run (quickstart):
  1) git clone && cd examples/tailor
  2) ./scripts/setup-local-index.sh # builds tiny sqlite index store and sample docs
  3) ./scripts/dev-server/start-replay.sh --seed samples/replays/faq-session.json
  4) open playground/index.html (TS shim) or run kotlin-client/gradlew :run (requires JDK 17)
  5) iterate on templates/contract.yaml and run ./scripts/dev-server/replay-check.sh to get deterministic output and CI-friendly diffs.

Checklist (PR):
  - [x] examples/tailor/ README + quickstart
  - [x] typed tool contract spec + codegen hooks (templates/contract.yaml + generator stubs)
  - [x] kotlin client demonstrating typed calls and structured-output parsing
  - [x] typescript playground shim with UI + structured-output linter
  - [x] offline indexer with incremental patch API and language-detection profiles
  - [x] devserver snapshot replay + simple CI smoke harness
  - [x] docs site snippet and linking to quickstarts page

Backward-compatibility and risk: no runtime changes to production services. All changes are example code, scripts, and docsite snippets. The only CI addition is a non-blocking smoke job (examples/tailor:smoke) which runs on the example repo; it is marked non-blocking on main.

Notes for maintainers: contract codegen is intentionally minimal; the generator stubs are commented with TODOs to show where teams should plug in their proto/kt/ts codegen. The offline indexer uses sqlite for portability and includes a small config for embedding provider selection; replace with your infra-backed store for large corpora.

Related work: references ENG-2147 (RAG dev ergonomics spike), several internal quickstarts on incremental-indexing. Also ties to docs site effort PM-401 to surface more JVM-first examples.

This description contains operational guidance, links to the quickstart, and step-by-step developer notes so new engineers can get a working loop in <10 minutes with local snapshots.
